topic.title: Decision-Tree Optimization, Interpretation, and Verification
topic.overview: Decision trees express predictions through successive tests, while ensembles combine many such structures. This topic studies finding compact accurate trees, understanding influential training examples, and verifying ensemble properties. It balances the simplicity of individual rules against the computational difficulty of optimizing or inspecting their combinations.
topic.whyItMatters: A small tree can make a decision process easier to follow, but greedily chosen splits may miss better structures. Large ensembles create a different challenge: readable components can still combine into complex behavior. Optimization and verification therefore require explicit objectives and careful accounting of search complexity.
topic.evolution: Early representative titles concern probabilistic classification and improvements to ID3. Later work studies sparse optimal trees and training-sample influence. SPLIT in 2025 uses lookahead where it matters and greedy choices near leaves; a 2026 verification framework searches combinations of tree outputs to test properties such as robustness or fairness.
openQuestions: How much predictive flexibility can compact trees retain while remaining understandable?
When can ensemble verification avoid enumerating exponentially many output configurations?

papers.tldr: Multiple smaller predictors with optimized backup filters improve learned Bloom filter performance within the same memory budget.

papers.title: Generalized additive models via direct optimization of regularized decision stump forests
papers.tldr: Directly optimizing regularized stump forests produces generalized additive models with competitive accuracy and fewer parameters.

papers.title: Generalized Random Forests Using Fixed-Point Trees
papers.tldr: Fixed-point trees avoid Jacobian estimation in generalized random forests, improving speed while preserving statistical guarantees and reported accuracy.

papers.title: Learning Minimum-Size BDDs: Towards Efficient Exact Algorithms
papers.tldr: A witness-tree-based algorithm improves exact BDD minimization when diagram size, domain size, and pairwise data differences are small.

papers.title: Leveraging Predictive Equivalence in Decision Trees
papers.tldr: A Boolean representation of decision boundaries resolves predictive equivalence in trees and supports better analysis of missing values, variable importance, and prediction cost.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Decision Trees in a SPLIT Second
papers.tldr: SPLIT uses greedy decisions near tree leaves to achieve orders-of-magnitude speedups with negligible reported performance loss.

papers.title: On the Power of Learning-Augmented Search Trees
papers.tldr: Prediction-weighted treap priorities yield robust, dynamic search trees with optimality guarantees extending to arbitrary access distributions.

papers.title: Optimal Decision Tree Pruning Revisited: Algorithms and Complexity
papers.tldr: Optimal decision-tree pruning is polynomial-time for subtree replacement but NP-complete for subtree raising, with tractability depending on combined input parameters.

papers.title: A faster training algorithm for regression trees with linear leaves, and an analysis of its complexity
papers.tldr: An exact reformulation accelerates TAO training and explains why sufficiently deep regression trees can become faster to train as they grow.

papers.title: Empowering Decision Trees via Shape Function Branching
papers.tldr: Shape Generalized Trees use visualizable nonlinear feature functions to make compact decision trees.

papers.title: Improving Decision Trees through the Lens of Parameterized Local Search
papers.tldr: Local decision-tree improvement is NP-complete generally but becomes fixed-parameter tractable when feature count and domain size are jointly bounded.

papers.title: Learning Gradient Boosted Decision Trees with Algorithmic Recourse
papers.tldr: A recourse-aware boosting algorithm makes reasonable prediction-changing actions available for more instances while preserving accuracy and computational efficiency in experiments.

papers.title: Regression Trees Know Calculus
papers.tldr: For differentiable target functions, regression-tree parameters provide efficient gradient estimates that support sensitivity analysis, uncertainty quantification, and interpretation.

papers.title: SORTeD Rashomon Sets of Sparse Decision Trees: Anytime Enumeration
papers.tldr: SORTD efficiently enumerates similarly performing sparse decision trees in objective order, making useful alternatives available throughout the search.

papers.title: Tree Ensemble Explainability through the Hoeffding Functional Decomposition and TreeHFD Algorithm
papers.tldr: TreeHFD estimates a tree ensemble’s Hoeffding decomposition, separating main effects and interactions while accommodating dependent inputs.

papers.title: CLARITree: Cholesky and Lookahead Accelerations for Regression with Interpretable Piecewise Linear Trees
papers.tldr: CLARITree combines lookahead search with efficient matrix updates to build sparse, near-optimal piecewise linear regression trees.

papers.title: Correcting Split Selection in Online Decision Trees via Anytime-Valid Inference
papers.tldr: Anytime-valid split tests repair statistical guarantees for streaming decision trees and yield better-performing, smaller trees in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Decision Tree Learning on Product Spaces
papers.tldr: The paper extends greedy decision-tree guarantees to arbitrary product distributions and introduces an algorithm needing no prior size or depth parameters.

papers.title: Exact and Approximate Algorithms for Polytree Learning
papers.tldr: The paper improves exact polytree learning under constant in-degree bounds and provides polynomial-time approximations with provable quality guarantees.

papers.title: From Rashomon Theory to PRAXIS: Efficient Decision Tree Rashomon Sets
papers.tldr: PRAXIS efficiently approximates collections of near-optimal decision trees, regularly recovering almost all of the full set in validation.

papers.title: OC-space: a Unifying Perspective on Verification of Tree Ensembles
papers.tldr: OC-space expresses diverse tree-ensemble verification tasks as searches over output configurations, offering practical speedups despite potentially exponential space size.

papers.title: PINE: Pruning Boosted Tree Ensembles with Conformal In-Distribution Prediction Equivalence
papers.tldr: PINE improves tree-ensemble compression by guaranteeing prediction equivalence within a conformally calibrated in-distribution region.

papers.title: Theoretical Challenges in Learning for Branch-and-Cut
papers.tldr: Theoretical examples show that accurate local branch-and-cut scores can still lead to exponentially larger search trees.
